title: Bimodal Pore Engineering of Mesoporous Carbon onto Ti3C2T x via a Soft–Hard Templating Route for Highly Durable Potassium-Ion Batteries
abstract: Abstract Two-dimensional mesoporous carbon materials with tailored porosity and robust interfacial coupling are pivotal for potassium-ion batteries, yet the precise construction of bimodal pores remains a critical bottleneck. Herein, we propose an interfacial assembly strategy for the in situ growth of N,P-co-doped bimodal mesoporous carbon onto Ti3C2Tx MXene (D-NMC/Ti3C2Tx) via a phytic acid (PA)-mediated soft–hard dual-templating route. Both theoretical and experimental results demonstrate that PA serves as a molecular bridge, reinforcing hydrogen-bonding interactions to orchestrate the coassembly of P123, SiO2 nanospheres, and 2,6-diaminopyridine onto the functionalized Ti3C2Tx surface. Attributed to the unique design, D-NMC/Ti3C2Tx delivers a high reversible capacity of 303.6 mAh g–1 at 0.1 A g–1 over 200 cycles and retains 148.3 mAh g–1 after 3500 cycles at 1.0 A g–1. XPS depth profiling reveals that the enhanced performance originates from a stable inorganic-rich solid electrolyte interphase that maintains electrode integrity. This work offers a promising strategy for designing advanced carbon-based electrodes.

title: Preparation and Electrochemical Performance Study of Covalent Organic Framework-Derived Porous Carbon@FeS2
abstract: Abstract Covalent organic frameworks (COFs) offer designable skeletons and ordered pore domains, but poor charge transport and insufficient electrochemically active sites hinder their direct use as electrodes. In this work, COF-Bq was first obtained by Knoevenagel condensation and then transformed by carbonization and KOH activation into COF-BqC-700-3. A hydrothermal step grew FeS₂ within and on this porous carbon, giving COF-BqC-700-3@FeS₂ composites. The optimized COF-BqC-700-3@FeS₂-160-2 maintained hierarchical porosity dominated by micropores and reached 740.2 F g⁻¹ at 1 A g⁻¹. When assembled with COF-BqC-700-3 in an asymmetric device, it delivered 25.03 Wh kg⁻¹ at 750 W kg⁻¹. The device retained 90.95% capacitance after 5,000 cycles and showed 99.93% Coulombic efficiency. These results show that FeS₂ adds Faradaic storage sites to COF-derived carbon while the porous carbon framework supports charge transfer and ion transport.

title: Mesoporous curvature-induced proton coupled electron transfer for rapid photoredox of CO2 to CH4
abstract: Abstract The photoreduction of CO 2 is usually terminated by two-electron processes resulting in predominantly products CO, the formulation of eight-electron products CH 4 still remains a great challenge limited by proton coupled electron transfer (PCET) abilities. Here, a novel type of two-dimensional (2-D) mesoporous TiO 2 (mTiO 2 ) has been synthesized based on the nanoscale titanium-oxo cluster units for rapid photoredox of CO 2 to CH 4 . In this unique 2-D structure, a mesoporous sheet with ~ 2.7 nm in thickness and several micrometers in size, can be stably formed into uniform hexagonal arrays. The size of the mesopores can be precisely controlled from 8.0 to 18.0 nm by utilizing the amphiphilic di-block copolymer poly(styrene- block -acrylic acid) (PS- b -PAA) micelles with tunable block lengths. With a curvature-governed Ti 3+ density, such mesoporous sheets demonstrate excellent photocatalytic CO 2 reduction capability by accelerating the PCET processes, achieving a record-high CH 4 production rate of 0.49 mmol g − 1 h − 1 with near-unique selectivity up to 99.6% under full-spectrum solar irradiation, without sacrificial reagents and co-catalysts, and the 2-D mTiO 2 can retain their photocatalytic activity after five consecutive cycles. An equivariant geometric deep learning model was constructed to simulate the spin density of mesoporous TiO 2 , with the objective of identifying exposed active sites. Synchrotron X-ray absorption spectroscopy combined with EELS characterizations unambiguously verify that curved mesoporous interfaces induce reduced Ti − O coordination, concentrated oxygen vacancies and abundant low-valent Ti 3+ sites while retaining the anatase crystalline phase. Density functional theory (DFT) calculations confirm that curvature-enriched Ti 3+ sites can accelerate Volmer step and promote preferential hydrogenation to the carbon atom rather than oxygen (0.73 eV vs. 2.05 eV) due to a bent configuration of the Ti − O−Ti linkage. This atomic-scale selectivity suppresses CO formation and drives the reaction exclusively toward CH 4 , establishing a direct link between mesoporous curvature and multi-electron and proton coupling pathways. This work demonstrates that efficient and selective photocatalytic process can be achived by constructing rich Ti 3+ 2-D mesoporous structure via nanocluster assembly.

title: Bioinspired Buffered Microenvironment Enables Highly Crystalline 3D COF Gels With Controllable Structures for Exceptional Molecular Adsorption
abstract: ABSTRACT Reconciling long‐range crystallinity with macroscopic network formation remains a central challenge in constructing three‐dimensional covalent organic framework (3D COF) gels. Inspired by biomineralization and tofu coagulation, we propose a synergistic buffered system with salt bridges for direct assembly of crystalline 3D COF gels via imine condensation. Ten metal salts were selected to regulate stable and buffered pH microenvironment. Comparing various salts revealed a correlation between pH microenvironment and the formation state and crystallinity of COFs. NaAc emerges as representative regulator for multiple roles: (i) forming AcO − /AcOH buffer to maintain a stable weakly acidic microenvironment and promote disorder‐to‐order transition, (ii) regulating kinetics, defect healing, and COF topology, and (iii) Na + as salt bridges stabilizing the 3D gel network. Pore topology can be switched between two crystalline phases by varying side substituents and salt addition sequence, as seen by XRD peak shift from 8.9° to 6.6°. The gels have low density (0.028–0.042 g/cm 3 ), high compressive strength, CO 2 /N 2 selectivity of 140, organic solvent uptake up to 80 times their weight, and over 90% capacity retention after 20 cycles. Overall, this work establishes a paradigm from microenvironment engineering and ion selection to topology regulation and adsorption, providing a blueprint for functional 3D COF gels.

title: Fully Conjugated Chiral Covalent Organic Frameworks Enabling High‐Density Polaron Hopping Conduction via Spin‐Frustration Relief
abstract: ABSTRACT Organic semiconductors are key materials for high‐performance organic electronics, where both high carrier density and fast carrier mobility are required to achieve high conductivity. However, increasing carrier concentrations inevitably introduces scattering effect that severely impair charge transport. Here we report a strategy to synthesize highly polarized covalent organic frameworks (COFs) through chirality‐induced crystallization and a subsequent COF‐to‐COF transformation, yielding benzothiazole‐linked fully conjugated frameworks. The resulting porous organic crystals feature an enhanced polarization arising from the parallel stacking of benzothiazole moieties, which enables precise N‐over‐N and S‐over‐S atomic alignment across neighboring layers. Benefiting from anisotropic polarization, the chiral COF film exhibits an excellent intrinsic conductivity of 1.9 × 10 −2 S cm −1 , along with a high carrier concentration of 1.1 × 10 17 cm −3 and a fast carrier mobility of 1.1 cm 2 V −1 s −1 . Upon iodine doping, the optimal conductivity of the chiral COFs is enhanced by more than one order of magnitude compared to that of the achiral analog with antiparallel stacking. We provide insights into the polaron‐mediated conduction mechanism through electron‐phonon coupling in the axisymmetric polarized frameworks, which addresses the carrier‐scattering issue even at high carrier densities. Our findings establish highly polarized organic crystals as promising semiconductors for advanced electronics.

title: Site-Selective and Deuterium-Programmable Electrochemical Synthesis of Deuterated Pharmaceuticals
abstract: Abstract Deuterium labeling plays a pivotal role in pharmaceutical development by modulating physicochemical properties and enabling metabolic tracing. However, site-selective and programmable deuteration in amine-containing pharmaceuticals remains a formidable challenge, as it typically requires prefunctionalized and costly deuterated reagents that hamper scalability and practical utility. Here, we report an electrochemical strategy for synthesizing deuterated amine pharmaceuticals using D2O as a cost-effective deuterium source, enabling site selectivity, degree-programmable deuteration, and excellent deuterium incorporation. Central to this approach is the electrochemical conversion of toxic polyhalides into reactive deuterated building blocks in situ, facilitating the efficient synthesis of over 70 deuterated drugs, with selective mono-, di-, and trideuteration at the N-benzyl, N-methyl, O-benzyl, and S-benzyl positions, and broad functional-group tolerance. Collectively, we establish a platform integrating polyhalides valorization with precision isotopic editing for accessing high-value deuterated pharmaceuticals, especially amine-containing drugs bearing common metabolic soft spots such as benzyl and methyl motifs.

title: Guest‐Directed Navigation of a Ligand Conformational Landscape Enables Palladium‐Organic Cage–Bowl–Helicate Interconversion
abstract: ABSTRACT Biological systems regulate molecular function by reshaping conformational energy landscapes in response to external stimuli. Translating this principle into artificial supramolecular systems remains challenging, particularly when multiple structurally distinct states must be accessed using a single class of stimulus. Here, we report a conformationally adaptive ligand L comprising two 2,4,6‐tris(4‐pyridyl)‐1,3,5‐triazine (TPT) panels connected by a conformationally flexible 3,3′‐disubstituted biphenyl spacer. Coordination of L with (en)Pd(II) affords a discrete Pd 4 L 2 cage 1 . Distinct guests redirect the assembly landscape along divergent pathways: 6‐methylcoumarin ( G1 ) induces the bowl‐shaped Pd 4 L 2 complex ( G1 ) 4 ⊂ 2 , whereas 1‐adamantanol ( G2 ) selects the Pd 6 L 3 triple‐stranded helicate ( G2 ) 8 ⊂ 3 . Cage 1 , bowl 2 , and helicate 3 correspond to trans‐/cis‐, cis‐/cis‐, and cis‐/trans‐ combinations of the biphenyl spacer and TPT‐panel orientations, respectively. Guest‐exchange experiments reveal path‐dependent interconversion: G1 converts helicate 3 toward a mixture of cage 1 and bowl 2 , whereas guest removal restores cage 1 , enabling G2 to redirect it back to helicate 3 . Thus, the system can be precisely navigated among cage, bowl, and helicate architectures solely through guest addition, removal, and exchange. A 4,4′‐biphenyl‐linked analogue shows no comparable conversion. These results establish a guest‐addressable three‐state self‐assembly landscape in which distinct combinations of ligand cis‐/trans‐ conformations encode divergent supramolecular architectures.

title: From Sintering to Mineralization: A Liquid-Phase Growth Route for Ceramic Films
abstract: Abstract The fabrication of dense ceramic films for solid-state electronics and energy-conversion systems has long been hindered by a fundamental sintering dilemma: the high temperatures required to activate solid-state diffusion simultaneously promote elemental volatilization, interfacial reactions, and phase segregation. Inspired by natural mineralization, we develop a biomimetic liquid-phase growth (LPG) strategy that enables the direct formation of dense ceramic films under mild conditions. As a stringent model system, we select the highly refractory proton conductor BaZr0.85Y0.15O3−δ (BZY), which possesses a melting point of 2700 °C. In the LPG process, molten Ba(NO3)2 serves as both a reactive precursor and a liquid transport medium, while a (ZrO2)0.92(Y2O3)0.08 (YSZ) seed layer confines nucleation and directs interfacial crystal growth and coalescence. This strategy produces dense, chemically homogeneous BZY films at 600 °C, more than 1000 °C below those required in conventional solid-state sintering. The evolution mechanism of the LPG process is elucidated through in situ real-time characterizations. The versatility of this strategy is further demonstrated by the successful growth of BaHfO3, BaHfO3@BZY heterostructured, and SrZr0.85Y0.15O3−δ films. Fuel-cell tests validate the electrochemical functionality of the BZY-LPG electrolytes. By reconceptualizing film densification as a liquid-phase mineralization process, LPG establishes a distinct chemical framework for the low-temperature synthesis of dense films, substantially expanding the design landscape for advanced ceramic devices.

title: Processing-induced self-organised triboelectric interfaces enable event-responsive cementitious composites
abstract: Structural materials are commonly designed to bear loads passively, whereas sensing and energy-harvesting functions are typically implemented using externally attached devices that are vulnerable to damage and interfacial failure. Here we report a processing-induced strategy for forming self-organised triboelectric interfaces directly within fibre-reinforced cementitious composites during vibration-assisted casting. Through fresh-state flow, fibre migration, and grid-assisted interception, conductive and dielectric constituents assemble into local fibre-enriched contact regions, enabling intrinsic electromechanical transduction without post-fabrication assembly. Microstructural characterisation reveals local fibre enrichment and fibre-grid interweaving around the embedded coated grid, while first-principles calculations support the interfacial charge redistribution between polyvinyl alcohol and polytetrafluoroethylene. The composites retain high mechanical toughness while exhibiting stable electrical responses under low-frequency mechanical excitation, with signal amplitude scaling with load and contact configuration. After cracking, newly created internal interfaces continue to provide functional output, demonstrating damage-tolerant electromechanical activity. We further demonstrate an event-triggered sensing system in which the embedded interfaces serve as self-powered signal sources for wake-up and alert operations. This work establishes a processing-driven route for programming functional interfaces within structural materials and provides a basis for intrinsically responsive infrastructure components. The study shows that vibration-assisted casting forms fibre-polymer contacts inside a cementitious composite, enabling electrical signals after damage and a laboratory demonstration of event-triggered alerts.

title: Spiral-in-Shrink Assembly of Microarchitected Circularly Polarized Luminescent Networks
abstract: Abstract High-fidelity three-dimensional displays require precise control over the polarization of light. Screens incorporating chiral emissive micropixels─which allow effective regulation of spin angular momentum─offer the potential for minimal-crosstalk, high-definition imaging. However, such highly asymmetric luminous, densely integrated microarrays have not yet been reported, owing to interfacial pinning effects and easy chiral structural degradation during miniaturization. Here, we present a spiral-in-shrink assembly strategy that couples evaporation-induced contraction with chiral self-organization in a nonequilibrium pathway. Geometry-confined shrinkage and chiral helically ordered microdomes act in concert to stabilize circularly polarized emission, yielding lateral features of 58 μm─corresponding to a significant improvement in miniaturization over reported dimensions. Large-area arrays comprising over 31,000 emissive units achieve 359 pixels per inch─and luminescence dissymmetry factors up to 1.25, enabling densely packed full-color photonic patterning. Moreover, spatially encoded handedness distributions underpin polarization-resolved mapping on aerial platforms for human–machine sensing. Our scalable route establishes a platform for cohesive chiroptical materials across advanced optical displays, polarization imaging, and intelligent sensing.

title: Drug‐Stiffened Polymer Worms: Allostery‐Inspired Activity Gating and Endogenous Enzyme‐Recharged Catalytic Cycling
abstract: ABSTRACT Natural enzymes achieve efficient and specific catalysis through precise allosteric regulation, a dynamic interplay of conformational rigidity and flexibility that remains largely unrealized in synthetic catalysts. Here, we report an allostery‐inspired polymer assembly whose catalytic and therapeutic functions are gated by programmable changes in supramolecular rigidity. The assemblies initially form flexible worm‐like micelles, whereas drug loading induces coordination‐driven crystallization into rigid nanorods. This rigidification restricts substrate accessibility and electron transfer, concurrently suppressing its peroxidase‐like activity, drug cytotoxicity, and fluorescence. In the glutathione (GSH)‐rich tumor microenvironment, disruption of metal coordination reverses rigidification, restores the flexible morphology, and reactivates all functions. The activated assemblies then use tumor‐overexpressed NAD(P)H:quinone oxidoreductase 1 (NQO1) as an endogenous redox partner, channeling reducing equivalents from reduced nicotinamide adenine dinucleotide (NADH) to replenish their electron reservoir and enable repeated catalytic turnover. This NQO1‐recharged cascade depletes intracellular GSH and NADH while generating cytotoxic hydroxyl radicals, thereby inducing apoptosis, ferroptosis, and cuproptosis, triggering immunogenic cell death, and eliciting robust antitumor immunity in vivo. By integrating allostery‐inspired structure gating with endogenous‐enzyme‐driven catalyst recharging, this work establishes an adaptive catalytic platform that addresses limitations in the activity regulation and redox cycling of artificial enzymes and offers a strategy for catalytic cancer therapy.

title: Electron-Catalyzed Supramolecular Assembly with High Efficiency, Robustness, and Versatility
abstract: Abstract Although catalysis is widely exploited by nature to orchestrate noncovalent supramolecular assembly and build up complex living systems, its utilization in synthetic chemistry has conventionally been limited to accelerating covalent reactions. Consequently, the development of artificial systems for catalytic assembly remains a formidable and largely unexplored challenge. Here, we present a rationally designed strategy of electron-catalyzed supramolecular assembly, wherein the electron acts as an efficient, robust, and versatile catalyst to accelerate the formation of a donor–acceptor complex. Optimization of the elementary steps and intermediate stability yields an efficient catalytic cycle, furnishing the process with both a high turnover number and operational robustness in open air. Furthermore, the electron catalysis can be readily triggered by diverse external stimuli─including electricity, light, and mechanical force─enabling precise spatiotemporal control over the assembly process and near-quantitative synthesis of supramolecular complexes. Collectively, this work establishes a well-elucidated strategy of catalytic assembly with remarkable practicality, advancing the frontiers of noncovalent synthetic chemistry.

title: A trapped catalytic product acts as molecular glue for innate immune signalosome assembly
abstract: Innate immune systems of living organisms are essential for host defense. Central to these systems is the Toll/interleukin-1 receptor (TIR) domain, an evolutionarily conserved module. From antiphage systems in prokaryotes to innate immune systems in plants, TIR domains have catalytic activity. However, TIR domains within animal innate immune receptors, such as Toll-like receptors (TLRs), have been considered as scaffolds for adaptor recruitment. We report that the TLR4 TIR domain possesses an allosterically activated nicotinamide adenine dinucleotide (NAD + ) hydrolase (NADase) activity that operates in a single-turnover manner. Its product, adenosine diphosphate ribose, is not released but entrapped as a “molecular glue,” stabilizing a composite catalytic pocket with adaptor TIR domain–containing adaptor protein (TIRAP) to nucleate signalosome assembly. This “produce-and-trap” mechanism represents a signaling mode that integrates enzymatic activity with adaptor function to drive downstream signaling.

title: Mapping the Slow Propagation of Disorder across a Photoreceptor’s Tertiary Structure with Time-Resolved Crystallography
abstract: Abstract Order–disorder transitions allow many proteins to shift between compact and flexible/unfolded states, thereby acting as structural switches that regulate catalysis, signaling, recognition, and allostery. We applied time-resolved serial oscillation crystallography to establish the structural kinetics of the light-triggered order–disorder transition of an animal-like cryptochrome as a six-second-long molecular movie with near-atomic all-residue spatial resolution and millisecond temporal resolution. Our 29 structural snapshots mapped the propagation of disorder across the tertiary structure motifs of a cryptochrome’s C-terminal region, triggered by a single broken D321–R492 salt bridge. The order–disorder transition followed a nucleation-propagation mechanism reminiscent of helix–coil dynamics and proceeded over up to five seconds, with regions distal to the D321–R492 trigger initially undergoing slow zero-order disordering before switching to first-order unfolding kinetics. Our per-residue density analysis provides a detailed structural-kinetic basis for understanding how order–disorder transitions emerge through directional propagation across protein tertiary structures, as occurring in signaling and many other biological systems.

title: Identification of the Intrinsic Ordering Effect of PtCo Intermetallic Catalysts on Fuel Cell Durability
abstract: ABSTRACT The dissolution of 3d transition metals is a central bottleneck limiting the practical use of Pt‐alloy cathode catalysts in fuel cells. Although ordered intermetallic compounds (IMCs) have been explored for nearly 4 decades as a route to mitigate this instability, the durability benefit of structural ordering itself remains debated and has rarely been reliably validated under practical membrane electrode assembly (MEA) conditions. Herein, we design a phase‐diagram‐guided sequential annealing protocol that yields an ordered/disordered PtCo catalyst pair with closely matched particle size and composition, enabling the durability effect of structural ordering to be rigorously isolated. In practical MEAs, structural ordering does not translate into a significant H 2 ‐air performance gain but markedly slows catalyst degradation. For example, after 90 000 cycles of accelerated durability test, the ordered catalyst loses only 28 mV at 1.5 A cm −2 , less than half that of its disordered counterpart (65 mV). Correlative in situ MEA diagnostics, electron microscopy, and online inductively coupled plasma mass spectrometry trace this enhanced durability to suppressed Co outward diffusion and dissolution. Machine‐learning‐accelerated theoretical calculations further rationalize this stabilization by revealing a higher thermodynamic penalty for Co surface segregation and a larger kinetic barrier for Co diffusion toward neighboring vacancies in the ordered IMC.

title: Concise and Modular Access to a Chiral Biaryl Monophosphine Library and Downstream Use in Catalytic Enantioselective Transformations
abstract: ABSTRACT Atropoisomeric biaryl monophosphines, chiral variants of Buchwald‐type ligands, are powerful ligands for asymmetric catalysis. However, their synthesis relies heavily on resolution or step‐intensive synthetic approaches, restricting structural diversity and tuning options, thus limiting systematic exploration of their catalytic potential. We report a unified strategy for streamlined access to a broadly tunable family of atrop‐chiral biaryl monophosphines. The three‐step assembly protocol first exploits a Cp X ‐Ir III ‐catalyzed atroposelective C─H arylation of phosphine oxide to forge the biaryl core with three different diversity points. Subsequently, reduction to the phosphine and installation of the fourth diversity point provide a diverse library of 35 chiral air‐stable monophosphine ligands. Their catalytic performance was benchmarked in a challenging enantioselective gold‐catalyzed cycloisomerization and a palladium‐catalyzed asymmetric phenol dearomatization, leading to the discovery of high‐performing library members providing excellent enantioselectivities of up to 99:1 er in both transformations.

title: Late-Stage Fluorosulfurylation Using Sulfuryl Fluoride Bound within a Metal–Organic Framework
abstract: Abstract Organic S(VI) fluorides have garnered substantial interest for covalent drug discovery and chemoproteomics due to their ambient stability and unique electrophilic reactivity. Sulfuryl fluoride (SO2F2) is the ideal reagent for the synthesis of various S(VI)–F moieties, yet it is a toxic greenhouse gas, often making it incompatible with laboratory settings. Developing a strategy for handling SO2F2 that is amenable to high-throughput reaction discovery would enhance its utility in the laboratory without necessitating specialized equipment or extensive safety measures. Herein, we report a strategy to safely store reactive SO2F2 within a metal–organic framework (MOF) for its facile application to the synthesis of electrophilic, bioactive molecules. The solid SO2F2–Mg2(dobdc) reagent can be stored for at least five months with minimal gas loss due to the strong yet reversible interaction between SO2F2 and Mg2+ centers in the MOF, as confirmed by single-crystal X-ray diffraction. Using this reagent, we prepare a range of drug-like arylfluorosulfates, primary and secondary acyclic sulfamoyl fluorides, saturated N-heterocyclic sulfamoyl fluorides, and N-heteroarene sulfamoyl fluorides, the last of which cannot be accessed using sulfonium salt alternatives to SO2F2 due to the requirement for strongly basic conditions. These findings represent the first experimental study of SO2F2 adsorption within a MOF and the first use of MOFs for late-stage fluorosulfurylation, paving the way toward a general approach to carefully handling dangerous, reactive gases as solid reagents.

title: Energy-efficient atmospheric water harvesting using MOF-801 and microwave-synthesized Al-fumarate: linking micro–mesoporous structure to sorption and regeneration behavior
abstract: Abstract Atmospheric water harvesting (AWH) has emerged as a promising route to mitigate freshwater scarcity in arid and semi-arid regions. Existing studies typically evaluate individual metal–organic frameworks (MOFs) under limited conditions, leaving a gap in comparative assessments that link pore architecture to sorption behavior. This work aims to establish a direct, climate-relevant comparison between MOF-801 and Al-fumarate, for AWH applications. The sorbents were synthesized and characterized using XRD, FTIR, BET, SEM, and TGA to elucidate their structural and textural properties. Water vapor adsorption–desorption performance was quantified under controlled relative humidity and temperature, supported by thermodynamic analysis of the isosteric heat of adsorption. MOF-801 demonstrated higher water uptake at moderate humidity (0.247 g H 2 O g − 1 at 40% RH and 20°C), while Al-fumarate showed enhanced performance under more humid conditions (0.278 g H 2 O g − 1 at 80% RH and 25°C). Both sorbents were regenerated at ~ 80°C, corresponding to an energy requirement of 1.2–1.5 MJ L − 1 . Thermodynamic analysis indicated a higher initial isosteric heat of adsorption (Q st ) for MOF-801, consistent with stronger water-framework interactions in drier atmospheres, whereas Al-fumarate exhibited a flatter Q st profile favorable for humid conditions. Both materials were further evaluated in four-month field tests in contrasting humid (Rasht) and arid (Isfahan) climates to assess cycling stability. The results providing practical guidelines for selecting energy-efficient MOFs tailored to specific climatic conditions

title: Linker Steric Hindrance-Induced Defect Engineering Enables Oxygen Vacancy-Rich MOFs for Pollutant Degradation
abstract: Abstract The widespread contamination of water by emerging contaminants (ECs) demands the development of efficient remediation technologies. Although advanced oxidation processes reliant on reactive oxygen species (ROS) show promise, they typically depend on energy- or reagent-intensive activation methods. Here, we introduce a linker steric hindrance-induced defect engineering (LSH-DE) strategy for metal–organic frameworks, which enables catalytic ROS generation using molecular oxygen (O2) as a benign terminal oxidant at ambient temperature and pressure. By systematically modulating the steric bulk of organic linkers, we precisely create missing-linker defects and direct the formation of oxygen vacancy (Vo) in robust Ce-UiO-66 during a rapid 15 min synthesis. Spectroscopic and computational analyses confirm that these oxygen vacancies promote O2 adsorption and activation to yield superoxide radicals (•O2–). The optimized catalyst, Ce-UiO-66-(CH3)2, demonstrates superior activity in degrading ubiquitous ECs without requiring external energy inputs or chemical mediators. Furthermore, integration of Ce-UiO-66-(CH3)2 into a membrane-based recirculating flow-through system enabled sustained water treatment, maintaining &gt;90% BPA removal over 48 h with a high water permeance of 101.5 L m–2 h–1 bar–1. This work presents a general and sustainable approach for designing catalytic defects in MOFs, advancing the development of green, next-generation water purification technologies.

title: Covalent Organic Frameworks for Exceptional Removal of PFAS From Water
abstract: ABSTRACT Per‐ and polyfluoroalkyl substances (PFAS) are persistent contaminants found globally in water, soil, and food, raising widespread public concern because of their high toxicity and the risks they pose to the environment and human health. Although considerable efforts have been devoted over the past decades to developing materials for PFAS removal from water, lowering PFAS to regulation‐compliant concentrations remains a formidable challenge. Here, we report covalent organic frameworks (COFs) engineered through a geometry‐specific strategy for PFAS capture from water. This approach installs peapod‐shaped pairs of closely spaced quaternary ammonium cationic sites, generating cooperative binding pockets that maximize electrostatic interactions with PFAS. The frameworks display ultrafast uptake kinetics, exceptional capture efficiency across ten different PFAS, ultralow equilibrium concentrations, robust regenerability, and cycling stability. Notably, the resulting COF reduces the perfluorooctanoic acid concentration from 1000 to 3.85 ng L −1 in batch systems within 10 min and decrease to as low as 0.82 ng L −1 under flow operations, both surpassing the state‐of‐the‐art materials. These findings establish COFs as a powerful platform for programming pore environments and open an avenue toward unparalleled porous materials for PFAS removal and water treatment.

title: An Experimental MOF-Polymer Latent Space for Composite Design
abstract: Abstract Metal–organic frameworks (MOFs) have tremendous promise for filtration, catalysis, and sequestration, but they are limited by the polymer matrices in which they must be embedded to form functional composites. Here, we find an experimental approach in which composite performance can be predicted using a single MOF particle. In particular, we attach single MOF particles to atomic force microscope (AFM) probes and find that the forces between the MOF-tipped probe and polymer films can be transformed into an instructive low-dimensional descriptor of MOF-polymer interactions. This two-dimensional latent space provides direct measures of chemical compatibility as well as the work of adhesion and can be used to understand interfacial phenomena in MOF-polymer composites. For example, polymer intercalation is observed via X-ray scattering for MOF-polymer combinations with high chemical-compatibility latent-space variables. Bulk composite performance can also be predicted using the latent space values for cases where the MOF is held constant. For example, a simple linear model was trained to predict CO2 absorption into composites of UiO-66-NH2 based solely on the latent space variables. In addition to providing a rapid way to screen polymer matrices to complement a MOF chosen for its bulk properties, these results suggest that composite performance may be a separable function of bulk properties and the interfacial latent space. In this way, this transfer-learning approach can vastly accelerate the design and understanding of functional composites.

title: Discovery of NIR-II nanocrystals Ag3AuSe2 with near-unity quantum yield
abstract: ABSTRACT The development of second near-infrared (NIR-II) emitting nanocrystals (NCs) with unity photoluminescence quantum yield (PLQY) is paramount for deep-tissue bioimaging and high-efficiency optoelectronics; however, the PLQY decreases markedly as the emission shifts to longer wavelengths. Herein, we have discovered a novel Ag3AuSe2 (fischesserite) NC system that extends this PLQY-wavelength frontier into the long-wavelength regime, achieving a near-unity absolute PLQY of 98.9% at 1000 nm with a monoexponential decay time of 4.1 µs. The synthesis of the near-single-crystal Ag3AuSe2 NCs hinges on the employment of an Au(I)-octanethiolate coordination polymer, [Au(OTT)]n, as the Au precursor. This precursor enables the regulated release of active gold species and provides a mild redox environment, which are essential for improving crystal quality and suppressing interfacial defects otherwise induced by side reactions. The exceptional brightness of these NCs provides a new paradigm for ultra-high signal-to-noise ratio imaging, fundamentally reshaping the application landscape for NIR-II emitters.

title: Multidimensional Protein-Based Antimicrobial Materials: Construction, Mechanisms, and Applications
abstract: Abstract Bacterial contamination and associated infections remain persistent threats to global public health. Proteins, as renewable biomacromolecules with diverse functional groups, programmable hierarchical structures, and favorable biocompatibility, have emerged as versatile building blocks for antimicrobial materials. Through self-assembly, amyloid-like aggregation, interfacial engineering, and chemical or physical functionalization, proteins can be constructed into zero-dimensional (0D) micro/nanoparticles, one-dimensional (1D) fibers, two-dimensional (2D) films and coatings, and three-dimensional (3D) hydrogels, aerogels, and sponge scaffolds. Dimensional architecture extends beyond morphological classification: it governs active-site exposure, interfacial contact, mass transport, mechanical properties, and antimicrobial-agent retention and release, thereby determining bactericidal activity, resistance to bacterial adhesion, and antibiofilm performance. Nevertheless, the relationships connecting dimensional construction, interfacial structure, antimicrobial mechanism, and application-specific performance remain fragmented. This review therefore adopts dimensionality as the central framework for critically examining the structural design, assembly, and functionalization of protein-based antimicrobial materials across 0D–3D architectures. Particular emphasis is placed on how dimensional features regulate the antimicrobial mechanisms involving membrane disruption, cell-wall hydrolysis, reactive oxygen species generation, physical bacterial trapping, controlled antimicrobial release, and resistance to bacterial adhesion. Recent advances in the applications of these antimicrobial materials, categorized by their dimensional architectures, are further evaluated across biomedicine, food preservation, functional textiles, and agriculture in relation to their operating environments and functional requirements. Finally, challenges concerning mechanistic validation, long-term stability, scalable manufacturing, biological safety, and application-specific evaluation are critically discussed to identify barriers to practical implementation and future directions for technological translation. Emerging opportunities in AI-assisted protein and peptide design, precise interfacial engineering, and multifunctional integration are further highlighted to guide the rational development of next-generation protein-based antimicrobial materials.

title: A Rutin–Glycyrrhizic Acid Self-Assembled Nanohydrogel Promotes Early Osteogenic Differentiation Potential and Antioxidant Activity via Synergistic Inhibition of the IL-1β/NF-κB Axis
abstract: Plant-derived natural compounds have gained increasing attention in biomaterial development due to their intrinsic bioactivity and favorable biocompatibility. The anti-inflammatory, antioxidant, and osteogenic properties of rutin and glycyrrhizic acid have rendered them increasingly attractive candidates for therapeutic biomaterial development. However, their poor bioavailability significantly restricts their broad biomedical applications. Inspired by a supramolecular self-assembly strategy, we successfully constructed a rutin-glycyrrhizic acid nanohydrogel (RU-GA). The microstructure and formation mechanism were investigated through experimental characterization and computational simulations. Rutin (RU) and glycyrrhizic acid (GA) self-assemble into a carrier-free hydrogel in aqueous solution via hydrogen bonding and π-π stacking interactions, exhibiting favorable injectability, shapeability, and stability. RU-GA can disperse in water and release rutin-glycyrrhizic acid nanoparticles (RG NPs) with homogeneous particle sizes, while the hydrogel material possesses degradation and sustained-release properties. The bioavailability of RU and GA is synergistically improved through size effects and continuous release. Notably, the RU-GA hydrogel significantly promotes antioxidant activity and early osteogenic differentiation potential relative to the individual monomer components. Bioinformatics analysis further suggested that these bioactivities are associated with IL1B. Il1b knockdown experiments validated that RU and GA may synergistically suppress IL-1β-mediated NF-κB activation, thereby reducing oxidative stress and enhancing early osteogenic differentiation potential. Collectively, the rutin-glycyrrhizic acid nanohydrogel (RU-GA) represents a promising functional biomaterial, providing a strategy for the broad application of natural compounds in biomedical and related fields.

title: Defect-Tolerant Frenkel Exciton Delocalization in Supramolecular Nanotubes
abstract: Abstract Preserving exciton delocalization in the presence of structural and environmental disorder is a central challenge for nanoscale photonic and optoelectronic materials. Here we show that Frenkel excitons in two-dimensional supramolecular nanostructures retain extensive delocalization even in the presence of intentionally incorporated deep-energy traps. Fluorescent trap molecules introduced during the self-assembly of double-walled molecular nanotubes provide a controlled model system in which strong local energetic perturbations are created without significant distortion of the host structure. Increasing the trap concentration shortens the host-exciton PL lifetime from ∼190 ps to ∼15 ps, while polarization-resolved microscopy of individual nanotubes shows that the collective excitonic polarization remains essentially unchanged. Frenkel-exciton calculations based on experimentally established molecular structures reproduce this robustness and reveal that delocalization decreases only weakly because the excitonic wave functions redistribute around the trap sites while remaining extended over large molecular domains. These results demonstrate an intrinsic defect tolerance of delocalized Frenkel excitons in a two-dimensional supramolecular architecture and identify dimensionality as an important design principle for preserving collective excitonic states in structurally imperfect nanomaterials.

title: A Solution‐Processable Single‐Component Molecular Antiferromagnet
abstract: ABSTRACT Developing solution‐processable molecular materials with long‐range magnetic order remains a formidable challenge for molecular electronic and spintronic applications. Herein, we present a diethoxybenzene‐fused neutral‐radical gold dithiolene complex, Au(4OEt) , as a solution‐processable single‐component molecular antiferromagnet. Owing to its ethoxy substituents, Au(4OEt) adopts a two‐dimensional (2D) herringbone arrangement and exhibits semiconducting behavior characteristic of a Mott insulator. Magnetic susceptibility, solid‐state 1 H NMR, and magnetic torque measurements reveal the emergence of long‐range canted antiferromagnetic (CAF) order below approximately 8 K. Combined with transfer‐integral calculations and magnetic analyses, these results suggest that constructing a 2D herringbone arrangement of neutral‐radical molecules with dominant 2D exchange interactions (| J 2 | > | J 1 |) is important for stabilizing the magnetic ordering. Leveraging its solubility, we successfully fabricated solution‐processed crystalline thin films that retain the CAF phase. Moreover, the crystalline thin film functions as an ambipolar field‐effect transistor (FET). This work thus provides a remarkable example of a solution‐processable single‐component molecular antiferromagnet exhibiting ambipolar FET characteristics, and establishes a structural design strategy for realizing magnetically ordered crystalline thin films toward future antiferromagnetic devices.

title: Molecularly Programmed Stress Dissipation Strategy for Ultrastretchable Neuromorphic Electronics
abstract: ABSTRACT Intrinsically stretchable organic synaptic transistors (ISOSTs) using semiconducting polymers (SPs) hold promise for on‐body signal processing by mimicking biological synaptic functions and processing temporal bio‐signals directly at or near the point of data acquisition. However, conventional SPs designed primarily to increase polymer softness and mechanical compliance often lack molecular‐level mechanisms for effective stress dissipation, thereby limiting device‐level stretchability to below 100% and causing substantial degradation in electrical performance. Here, we demonstrate ISOSTs achieving 150% device‐level stretchability through molecularly programmed stress dissipation (MPSD) of an SP without incorporating soft segments into the backbone. This strategy promotes conformational flexibility and suppresses side‐chain interdigitation, enhancing chain dynamics and amplifying mechanical contrast between crystalline and amorphous domains. This facilitates localized stress accommodation and induces the formation of nano‐to‐micro scale crack clusters, termed artificial stretch marks (ASMs), which emulate the adaptive mechanical behavior of human skin. Leveraging this mechanism, ISOSTs maintain 83.8% of maximum current even under 150% strain while preserving synaptic behaviors. Furthermore, physical reservoir computing using the ISOSTs preserves electromyography classification performance under 150% tensile strain. This work presents a biomimetic stress dissipation strategy for intrinsically stretchable and stress‐adaptive neuromorphic electronics.

title: Aligned graphene frameworks enabling high-thermal-conductivity phase-change thermal storage composites
abstract: Phase change materials (PCMs) offer high thermal storage density, but their low intrinsic thermal conductivity limits rapid thermal charging and discharging. Incorporating thermally conductive fillers can enhance heat transfer but generally reduces latent heat capacity, creating a trade-off between thermal conductivity and energy storage density. Constructing continuous and aligned heat-transfer pathways offers a promising strategy to alleviate this trade-off by improving thermal conductivity at lower filler loadings. Graphene, with its high in-plane thermal conductivity, is an attractive building block for such pathways. However, the effective thermal conductivity of graphene-based phase change composites (PCCs) remains far lower than the theoretical value owing to multiple limiting factors. Focusing on this challenge, this review adopts an integrated multiscale analytical framework to explore how the intrinsic thermal transport potential of graphene can be more effectively utilized in aligned graphene-based PCCs. It first examines graphene’s intrinsic thermal transport properties and their influencing factors, then systematically summarizes aligned assembly strategies and introduces a loading-normalized metric for supplementary assessment of graphene utilization efficiency. Furthermore, strategies for reducing thermal resistance at intersheet junctions and graphene–matrix interfaces are discussed to address another key limitation of macroscopic thermal transport. Recent applications in energy storage and conversion and advanced thermal management are also reviewed. Finally, it highlights key challenges and future research directions for improving thermal performance, ensuring long-term reliability, and enabling scalable fabrication.

title: Bioinspired Architected Materials for Aging‐Competent Brain Organoids: Multiscale Design, Assembly, and Translation
abstract: ABSTRACT Human brain organoids provide models of neural development and disease, but their developmentally young state and incompletely organized microenvironment limit the reconstruction of late‐life neural tissue. This review frames aging‐competent brain organoids as biohybrid architected systems in which cellular composition, extracellular matrices, material interfaces, transport pathways, and sensing or actuation modules are organized across length scales. An architecture–property–exposure–function framework is developed to connect matrix mechanics and ligand presentation, bioelectronic interfaces, vascular and oxygen‐regulating systems, redox‐active materials, programmable carriers, and nanosensors with tissue responses. Aging competence is defined as the capacity of a mature organoid to undergo reproducible, cell‐type‐resolved age‐associated transitions and to exhibit a progressive loss of homeostatic reserve after calibrated challenge. Accordingly, material‐enabled phenotypes are evaluated through molecular age, organelle flux, neurovascular and immune states, network performance, and challenge–recovery behavior, while excluding hypoxia, necrosis, acute toxicity, and material persistence as dominant explanations. The resulting design logic links multiscale assembly and multifunctionality to disease‐matched models of Alzheimer's disease, Parkinson's disease, amyotrophic lateral sclerosis/frontotemporal degeneration, and Huntington's disease, as well as to nanomedicine screening and translational qualification. Treating the organoid–material construct as an integrated architecture establishes functional materials as controllable modules for building, perturbing, monitoring, and therapeutically interrogating human brain aging.

title: A Series of TTDO-Based Energetic Cocrystals: From Supramolecular Assembly and Structural Analysis to Energetic Performance and Combustion Modulation
abstract: Abstract The inherent trade-off between high energy output and safety remains a critical bottleneck in the development of advanced propellants and high-energy-density materials. Here, we present a supramolecular assembly strategy using 2,4,6-triamino-1,3,5-triazine-1,3-dioxide (TTDO) as a Lewis base host to construct energetic cocrystals. Guided by COSMO screening, five nitro-containing Lewis acid energetic molecules were successfully cocrystallized with TTDO. Single-crystal X-ray diffraction reveals diverse protonation behaviors and extensive hydrogen-bonding networks, while electrostatic potential analysis shows that the positions of electrostatic potential extrema shift upon cocrystallization, correlating with significantly reduced mechanical sensitivity. Notably, TTDO-LLM-116 and TTDO-NMTT serve as multifunctional additives in ammonium perchlorate (AP)-based composite propellants. Incorporating only 10 wt % of these cocrystals merges the two-stage decomposition of AP into a single exothermic event and reduces the decomposition activation energy from 250.2 kJ·mol–1 to 107.4 kJ·mol–1 and 63.3 kJ·mol–1. Laser ignition experiments confirm enhanced combustion with a substantially shorter duration. As combustion additives, these cocrystals reduce the activation energy of AP while avoiding the energy-dilution effect commonly encountered with inert metal oxide catalysts. This work establishes TTDO-based cocrystals as a versatile platform for developing low-sensitivity, high-performance energetic materials, and advanced combustion modifiers for propellant applications.

title: Phylogeographic and functional assembly of population-level bacterial immunity
abstract: Bacterial pangenomes provide a shared reservoir of antiphage defenses, yet the ecological and functional constraints shaping this reservoir remain unclear. Here, we combine comparative genomics of 206 Xanthomonas oryzae pv. oryzae (Xoo) genomes with cross-infection assays of 50 strains against 36 phages and heterologous expression of 24 defense systems in a phage-sensitive Xoo chassis. The Xoo pan-defensome comprises a conserved core of 9 subtypes and a variable layer of 35 accessory and cloud subtypes structured by host phylogeography. Phages are more infectious on sympatric than allopatric hosts, consistent with local adaptation. Variable systems show stronger apparent activity than core systems, whereas resistance breadth is not predicted by defense system number. Co-expression of representative co-occurring and mutually exclusive system pairs reveals synergistic and antagonistic interactions underlying non-random repertoire assembly. Together, these findings extend the pan-immunity framework by showing that population-level immune reservoirs are shaped by both ecological structure and functional compatibility. In this study, the authors use comparative genomics and cross-infection assays to show a spatially and evolutionarily structured bacterial immune reservoir in which interactions among defense systems can reinforce or undermine phage resistance, refining the pan-immunity framework.

title: Swarm-inspired magnetic metal-organic framework-based microbots for on-demand moisture manipulation
abstract: Hygroscopic metal-organic frameworks (MOFs) are promising candidates for atmospheric water harvesting (AWH) and humidity control. Nevertheless, their practical application is often hindered by the poor manipulability of inherent powder forms and mass transfer limitations caused by the shaping. Drawing inspiration from the “hot defensive ball” aggregation morphology of honeybee swarms, a versatile magnetic shaping strategy hereby was reported to assemble MOF-based microbots, which enhances the formability of MOF powders. The obtained magnetic hygroscopic MOF (mMOF-303) exhibits enhanced water adsorption kinetics and enables efficient regeneration via multimodal heating strategies, including photothermal, electrothermal, and magnetothermal heating. Besides, the magnetic MOF-based microbots can change their aggregation patterns and perform directional motion according to application scenarios, enabling rapid water vapor sorption-desorption rates and precision confined space humidity control. This work provides a universal strategy to impart versatile formability to static MOF powders, paving the way for MOF engineering and advanced moisture management.

title: Raman-Inactive Metal–Organic Framework Nanoribbons as Plasmonic-Nanocavity Spacers and Molecular Trappers for SERS Detection
abstract: Abstract The integration of plasmonic nanostructures with metal–organic frameworks (MOFs) has emerged as a powerful strategy to enhance the sensitivity and selectivity of surface-enhanced Raman spectroscopy (SERS). While the resultant hybrid systems exploit localized surface plasmon resonance for electric-field enhancement and MOF porosity for molecular enrichment, their practical applications are hindered by challenges, including intrinsic Raman interference from MOFs, precise control over MOF dimensions, and restricted plasmon coupling configurations. Herein we present a promising design featuring Raman-inactive MOF nanoribbons embedded within plasmonic nanogaps between a gold film and gold nanospheres (NSs). The sub-10 nm MOF interlayer eliminates Raman background while maximizing electromagnetic enhancement. The resultant Au-film/MOF/NSs architecture enables remarkable SERS performances with enhancement factors of 1010 across diverse molecular sizes. This work not only enriches the toolbox of MOF-based plasmonic sensing platforms, but also opens the way for further exploration into other Raman-inactive MOFs and mechanisms.

title: Hydrogen-Bonded Organic Frameworks@Bacterial Cellulose Mixed-Matrix Membranes for Pollution Elimination
abstract: Abstract Hydrogen-bonded organic frameworks (HOFs) represent promising porous photocatalytic candidates for water remediation, yet their practical deployment is severely hindered by their powdery nature, poor machinability, and limited recyclability. Herein, we report a facile in situ growth strategy to immobilize methyl-modified (HOF-101-CH3), fluorine-modified (HOF-101-F), and pristine HOF-101 nanocrystals within the three-dimensional interconnected nanofibrous network of bacterial cellulose (BC), yielding HOFs@BC mixed-matrix membranes (MMMs). Robust interfacial hydrogen bonding and physical cross-linking are constructed between HOF crystallites and BC nanofibers, which effectively suppress HOF aggregation, improve mechanical tolerance, and grant the composite membrane favorable hydrophilicity for aqueous-phase operation. Benefiting from the electron-donating methyl substituent, HOF-101-CH3-m delivers a more negative surface zeta potential (–28.8 mV), elevated charge-carrier separation efficiency, and superior dye-selective performance. It achieved a high selectivity ratio of 49.5 (permeation flux: 174 L m–2 h–1 bar–1) toward mixed cationic methylene blue (MB) and anionic methyl orange (MO), with 99.1% MB removal and merely 2% MO adsorption. After five separation-regeneration cycles, the membrane retains a selectivity ratio above 41.5 and maintains approximately 84% of its initial selectivity performance. Under visible-light irradiation, abundant reactive oxygen species (1O2, ·OH, and H2O2) are generated by the embedded HOF-101-CH3, endowing the membrane with photocatalytic self-cleaning capability. Notably, HOF-101-CH3-m achieves complete photodegradation of bisphenol A (BPA) within 50 min and maintains 95.3% degradation efficiency over five cyclic photocatalytic runs. This work demonstrates a feasible structural-engineering route to transform intractable powdery HOFs into mechanically robust multifunctional membranes, offering insights into the future design of HOF-derived functional materials toward integrated selective dye separation and photocatalytic elimination of organic water pollutants.

title: Switching of Exciton-Polaritons in Covalent Organic Framework-Based Optical Resonators through Interaction with the Molecular Environment
abstract: Abstract We report a demonstration of a covalent organic framework (COF) integrated into an optical cavity for the realization of exciton–polaritons and their reversible switching through changes in the surrounding molecular environment. Films of COF nanoplates were integrated into Fabry–Pérot resonators engineered to achieve spectral matching between cavity modes and COF excitonic transitions, yielding strong light–matter coupling with a Rabi splitting above 300 meV. The cavity architecture preserves accessibility of the porous framework, enabling interaction with guest molecules. The potential of this interplay is shown by exposing the resonators to water vapor, which induces both a redshift and a pronounced reduction of the COF optical absorption. The observed hypochromic effect drives a reversible shift from strong to weak coupling, effectively switching exciton–polaritons on and off, as guest molecules are desorbed from or adsorbed in the reticular material host. The process is reversible upon desorption, with preservation of structural and optical integrity. These results establish COFs as a versatile platform for chemically tunable polaritonic systems, opening avenues for responsive photonic devices, sensing, and control of light–matter interactions in nanostructured materials.

title: Rational Synthesis of Sulfonic Acid-Functionalized Covalent Organic Frameworks for Selective Capture of Trace Strontium in Natural Mineral Water
abstract: Abstract As a typical long-lived radionuclide, strontium-90 (90Sr) possesses persistent radiological hazards and exhibits high migratory and diffusive behaviors in groundwater. However, the development of adsorbents for the efficient and highly selective capture of trace Sr(II) remains a great challenge. In this study, covalent organic frameworks (COFs, TpPa-2SO3H and TpPa-SO3H) with different numbers of sulfonic acid groups were rationally synthesized and applied for capturing Sr(II). The introduction of sulfonic acid groups onto TpPa-2SO3H and TpPa-SO3H endowed them with high adsorption capacities of 136.4 and 68.3 mg g–1 toward Sr(II), which were 12-fold and 6-fold higher than that of TpPa without sulfonic acid groups, respectively. Meanwhile, TpPa-2SO3H and TpPa-SO3H exhibited fast adsorption kinetics, capturing 99% of Sr(II) within 3 and 10 min, respectively. In addition, TpPa-2SO3H also exhibited high selectivity, excellent anti-interference performance, and regeneration ability without high calcium backgrounds. Characterizations and theoretical calculations demonstrated that sulfonic acid groups in TpPa-2SO3H promoted Sr(II) capture through strong ion-exchange interaction. TpPa-2SO3H was further applied to extract trace Sr(II) in natural Sr-containing mineral water samples. The results showed that the extraction efficiency for Sr(II) exceeded 95% within 5 min. Furthermore, the selectivity for Sr(II) was investigated by the distribution coefficients (Kd), and the Kd was 5.6 × 104 mL g–1 for TpPa-2SO3H toward Sr(II), approximately 400 times higher than those of Na(I) and K(I), respectively. This work not only developed a promising strategy to extract trace Sr(II) from real samples but also broadened the application of COFs in separation science.

title: Reticular Materials as Optical Sensors of Volatile Organic Compounds for Healthcare and Environmental Monitoring
abstract: Abstract Volatile organic compounds (VOCs) are a family of molecules that possess high vapor pressure and are regarded as air pollutants that prevail in both indoor and outdoor settings. Prolonged exposure to VOCs poses a serious risk to human health. On the other hand, VOCs emitted by humans and plants have been recognized as key biomarkers to estimate the status of health and physiology in living beings. Profiling the total content of VOCs in human and plant fluids leads to early diagnosis of diseases and timely treatment. Monitoring the presence of VOCs, either to track air pollution or to estimate the status of health, has therefore commanded increasing attention. Among the various techniques, optical sensing methods have been sought after owing to the considerations of their fast response time, versatility, miniaturization and portability, as well as the possibility of performing non-invasive detection. Advanced functional materials, such as porous reticular solids, including metal-organic frameworks (MOFs), covalent organic frameworks (COFs), and hydrogen-bonded organic frameworks (HOFs), are well suited not only as sorbents for the detection and capture of VOCs but also as suitable substrates for various approaches of optical signaling. This review, through recent case studies, presents the advances in the optical sensing of VOCs by reticular materials. In addition, a comparative analysis between various reticular material types has been provided, along with an outline of the current challenges and the opportunities that exist for future research.

title: Geometrically and chemically dual-adaptive COFs for selective recognition of multiple uranium species in complex waters
abstract: Sustainable uranium supply is critical for nuclear energy, yet its practical recovery is severely hindered by the chemical complexity of uranium in natural waters. In dynamic aqueous environments, uranium continuously shifts between large, cationic hydrolyzed clusters (acidic/neutral) and compact, anionic carbonate complexes (alkaline). Conventional static adsorbents fail to accommodate these contrasting charges and geometries. Here, we report a geometrically and chemically dual-adaptive three-dimensional covalent organic framework (COF), TAM-DTDA-AMM, to overcome this speciation barrier. Featuring a three-fold interpenetrated dia topology, the functional COF enables environment-driven reversible −COO−···NH4+ ion-pair reconfiguration, coupling adaptive pore-surface chemistry with dynamic spatial confinement. Under alkaline environments, cationic microdomains stabilize [UO2(CO3)3]4− via electrostatic and hydrogen-bonding interactions, whereas under near-neutral to acidic conditions, protonated carboxyl groups directly coordinate hydrolyzed uranyl clusters. This dual-adaptive mechanism enables rapid, selective, and high-capacity uranium extraction across diverse aqueous chemistries and offers a general strategy for recognizing multiple metal species in complex environments. Uranium recovery is hindered by the chemical complexity of uranium ions in natural waters. Here the authors report a geometrically and chemically dual-adaptive three-dimensional covalent organic framework which enables rapid and selective uranium-extraction across diverse aqueous chemistries.

title: Electric-field-assisted interfacial rubrene self-assembly for continuous tuning of liquid crystal pretilt angles
abstract: Abstract This study demonstrates a contact-free, low-temperature strategy for continuously tuning the pretilt angle of nematic liquid crystals (LCs) via electric-field-assisted capillary filling combined with rubrene self-assembly. By applying an AC electric field (0–5 V) across unrubbed, polyimide-free indium tin oxide (ITO) cells during LC injection, the pretilt angle of a rubrene-doped nematic LC mixture can be continuously programmed from approximately 3° (near-planar) to 90° (homeotropic). Contact-angle analysis reveals that increasing the filling voltage dramatically alters the interfacial interaction from a polar-dominated surface to a nonpolar, high-dispersive regime, resulting in a gradual transition from planar to homeotropic LC alignment. Electro-optical and dielectric measurements confirm stable, uniform LC alignment and customized threshold responses across cycles. This field-imprinted interfacial assembly method eliminates mechanical damage and high-temperature thermal processing, offering a scalable route for next-generation flexible, wearable, and tunable photonic devices

title: Machine learning techniques for understanding pattern formation and self-assembly in active colloidal systems
abstract: Abstract Active colloidal matter provides a rich setting for the emergence of nonequilibrium patterns, dynamic aggregates, and self-assembled structures. Understanding how such organization arises from microscopic interactions, fluctuations, and sustained external driving remains a central challenge in soft-matter physics. This is largely because traditional theoretical and computational approaches often struggle with nonlinear dynamics, multiscale behavior, and high-dimensional parameter spaces. In this context, machine learning (ML) is increasingly used to identify relevant order parameters, classify dynamical regimes, predict emergent structures, infer assembly pathways, and guide the design and control of target states. This review examines how ML methods are incorporated into the study of pattern formation and self-assembly across both equilibrium and active colloidal systems. The discussion is organized around the analysis and representation of data pertaining to complex nonequilibrium systems, the prediction of dynamical and structural outcomes, the inference of latent variables and assembly pathways, and the design or control of target states through generative models and&#xD;reinforcement learning strategies. We also discuss hybrid approaches that incorporate physical constraints to improve interpretability, robustness, and generalization. By focusing on the interplay between machine learning and nonequilibrium soft-matter physics, we highlight both the opportunities and the open challenges of the field, including the connection between learned representations and physical variables, limited extrapolation capability across state space, and the need for reproducible benchmarks and high-quality datasets. Overall, we argue that ML is emerging as an important complement to theory and simulation in the study of active colloidal self-assembly, not as a replacement for physical modeling, but as a means to accelerate discovery and deepen understanding of emergent nonequilibrium organization.

title: Skeletal Reconstruction of Tetrazole Rings Enables Synthesis of Fused Triazole–Pyrimidine Bicyclic Energetic Materials
abstract: Abstract Nitrogen-rich triazole-fused energetic materials featuring high heats of formation and extended π-conjugation represent crucial candidates for satisfying the dual requirements of high energy and exceptional insensitivity. However, achieving their effortless synthesis remains challenging. Herein, an efficient skeletal reconstruction strategy based on the thermal cleavage of tetrazole was utilized to synthesize a novel [5,6]-fused triazolopyrimidine explosive, TTO-1, and a plausible transformation mechanism was elucidated by theoretical calculations. Subsequent oxidation and self-assembly derivatization afforded a novel low-sensitivity energetic material, TTO-2, alongside a high-energy material, TTO-3. Both TTO-1 and TTO-2 possess favorable insensitivity (IS &gt; 50 J; FS &gt; 360 N) and detonation performance (P = 23.4 and 26.3 GPa, respectively), positioning them as promising candidates for low-sensitivity energetic materials, while TTO-3 displays a highly competitive detonation performance (P = 35.4 GPa). These findings provide valuable insights for the construction of advanced nitrogen-rich fused high-energy materials.

title: Sulfonated Poly(phenylene ethynylene) Redirects KLVFFAE Self-Assembly by Suppressing an α-Helix-like Intermediate
abstract: Peptides can assemble along different pathways, and the transient conformations they adopt along the way can influence the structure and properties of the final assemblies. How synthetic polymers alter these intermediate conformations and thereby control peptide assembly remains poorly understood. Here, we investigate how poly(phenylene ethynylene) bearing sulfonate side chains (PPE) changes the assembly pathway of the amyloid-β fragment KLVFFAE (KE). Time-resolved circular dichroism (CD) measurements showed that 50 μM KE in phosphate buffer at pH 4.25 first displayed α-helix-like features and later developed a spectrum characteristic of βsheet structure. Adding PPE markedly reduced the accumulation of the α-helical intermediate and accelerated the progression toward β-sheet-rich fibrillar assemblies. KE fully switched to this alternative pathway near the critical aggregation concentration of PPE, approximately 5 μM. Stopped-flow fluorescence measurements showed that mixing PPE with rhodamine B-labeled KE produced a rapid fluorescence decrease followed by a slower decay. We propose a two-step model in which electrostatic interactions contribute to the rapid association of PPE and KE, after which the resulting complex may undergo slower structural rearrangement. These findings show that PPE can redirect the assembly pathway of KE and suggest a two-step interaction process involving rapid electrostatic association followed by slower structural rearrangement. This provides a strategy for designing supramolecular peptide materials by controlling their assembly pathways.

title: Self-assembly versatility of N-acyl amino acids
abstract: N -acyl amino acids (NAAAs) are prebiotically plausible amphiphiles that can emerge from simple fatty acids and amino acids under abiotic conditions. As hybrid molecules combining two fundamental classes of prebiotic building blocks, NAAAs may have contributed to the emergence of structurally and functionally diverse molecular assemblies during early chemical evolution. However, how amino acid side chains influence their self-assembly behavior remains poorly understood. Here, we systematically investigated the self-assembly of three structurally distinct N -octanoyl amino acids— N -octanoyl-glycine (OA-G-OH), N -octanoyl-L-threonine (OA-T-OH), and N -octanoyl-L-phenylalanine (OA-F-OH)—to evaluate how amino acid side chains affect aggregation propensity and supramolecular structure. Our results indicate that NAAAs differ remarkably in aggregation propensity and generate distinct higher-order structures, potentially conferring functional diversity relevant to prebiotic chemistry and applications in drug delivery, biomedicine, and materials science.

title: Comparative One-Step Activation of Zhundong Coal Using KOH and ZnCl2: Hierarchically Porous Adsorbents for Malachite Green Adsorption
abstract: Abstract Although abundant in reserves, Zhundong coal is prone to severe slagging when combusted due to its high sodium content. Converting this coal into functionally designed carbon materials offers a sustainable strategy for clean utilization. This study compared hierarchically porous adsorbents prepared from Zhundong coal by one-step activation with ZnCl2 or KOH (denoted as ZnCl2@coal and KOH@coal, respectively) in terms of their pore structures and malachite green (MG) adsorption behavior in model aqueous solutions. Characterization revealed increased carbon content (from 67% to approximately 83%), specific surface area (from 10 to 1210–1773 m2/g), and pore volume of up to 1.00 cm3/g in both ZnCl2@coal and KOH@coal relative to the raw Zhundong coal. Adsorption experiments demonstrated that both adsorbents removed MG over the investigated pH range (2–9) and KCl concentrations (0–1000 mmol/L). The adsorption kinetics were well described by the pseudo-second-order model, whereas the Langmuir model fitted the equilibrium data better than the Freundlich model. Thermodynamic analysis indicated favorable MG adsorption under the adopted standard-state treatment and suggested a possible endothermic trend. At 308 K, the highest measured MG adsorption capacity of ZnCl2@coal was 5252.7 mg/g at an initial concentration of 6000 mg/L, while the Langmuir-derived maximum capacity was 8522.5 mg/g. Its higher MG uptake relative to KOH@coal at high initial concentrations was associated with a greater mesopore surface area and larger average pore width (2.77 nm versus 2.25 nm), although differences in surface chemistry and residual inorganic species may also contribute. This study provides a comparative assessment of KOH and ZnCl2 activation for converting low-grade Zhundong coal into porous adsorbents, highlighting the differences in the resulting materials’ physicochemical properties and MG adsorption behavior.
